extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors and referees for The College Mathematics Journal; college mathematics teachers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting manuscripts to The College Mathematics Journal, an expository peer-reviewed journal focused on undergraduate mathematics (esp. first two years). Covers scope, article types, formatting, and submission constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus / Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The College Mathematics Journal is an expository journal focused on mathematical topics inspired by the undergraduate mathematics curriculum, in particular, the first two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishes well-written and captivating articles that explore new mathematics or old mathematics in a new way and are aimed at college mathematics teachers and their upper-level students. Welcomes engaging writing, historical perspectives, and open questions; most articles are accessible to upper-level undergraduates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and Review Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The College Mathematics Journal only publishes manuscripts in English and has a double-anonymous review policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must submit English-language manuscripts and prepare them consistent with double-anonymous review (i.e., remove identifying information as required by the journal's policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted Article Types (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The College Mathematics Journal accepts the following types of articles: Articles, Classroom Capsules, Problems and Solutions, Proofs Without Words, Media Highlights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should choose the article type that best fits their contribution and follow the specific guidance and templates for that type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articles (full expository pieces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-crafted articles that explore new or innovative perspectives on both new and existing mathematics, most of which are accessible to upper-level undergraduates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize clear exposition, interest to college mathematics teachers, accessibility to upper-level undergraduates, and engaging writing; historical perspectives and open questions are welcomed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom Capsules
rubrics_metrics.description: A Classroom Capsule is a short article, typically 1-3 pages in length, that contains new insight on a topic taught in undergraduate mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably the Capsule should be something that can be directly introduced into a college classroom as an effective teaching strategy or tool. Use the Classroom Capsule template and the CMJ LaTeX style file when preparing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems and Solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem submissions must be original problems accompanied by solutions and should appeal to CMJ readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted problems should not be under consideration for publication elsewhere and must include solutions at the time of proposal/submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs Without Words
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs Without Words is an accepted submission type (visual/concise mathematical illustrations of proofs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use the Proof Without Words template together with the CMJ LaTeX style file before uploading a submission. Follow the concise visual nature of the format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Highlights
rubrics_metrics.description: Media Highlights are short reviews (up to half a page) intended to help readers monitor a broad spectrum of publications, web materials, professional activities, and instructional resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be brief (up to 1/2 page) and focus on items of interest to the mathematical community and colleagues; submit appropriate items that will be helpful for readers to monitor the landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting requirement: LaTeX style file and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Please download and use the LaTeX Style File with the article, Classroom Capsule, and Proof Without Words templates before uploading your submission to The College Mathematics Journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare manuscripts using the provided CMJ style file and the specific template for the intended article type to ensure correct formatting and facilitate review/production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refereeing guidance (reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a 'Guide for Referees' for those reviewing submissions for The College Mathematics Journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees should consult the Guide for Referees link for detailed expectations; the page points referees to that resource for standards and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprint Permission for MAA Institutional Members
rubrics_metrics.description: General permission is granted to institutional members of the MAA for noncommercial reproduction in limited quantities of individual articles (in whole or in part) provided a complete reference is made to the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reprint permission beyond this, or to request formal permission, authors/others should request permission from Taylor and Francis using the provided form.
